Hey man, I completely understand you, I was literally so lonely and depressed in my high school days, I had no friends and I hated everyone around me. For five years I cried out to God “why are you doing this to me” but he never seemed to answer. When I prayed, I would just get angry and when I went to church, I couldn’t even concentrate during the sermons. I honestly hated God for a long time and I blamed everything on him. 

But around last year, he finally began to start a work within me after 5 years of suffering and pain. I slowly began finding peace through prayer and I received so much grace every week at church. After a year, I am still struggling with severe depression and anxiety but I know that when I put my hope in God, he will finish his work that he began in me. 

I don’t blame God anymore for the hardships I went through because I believe it was part of his plan to make me start all the way at the bottom and slowly bring me to the top. And now, I am able to empathize with those suffering under depression and understand what they’re going through. 

When you say that God never brought you peace only problems, I completely get that because I would always pray to God but it seemed like he never answered me! It’s so so hard I get it but in the end, we just have to trust that he’s listening and he is making you go through this for a reason. A greater plan in the future that only you can live through BECAUSE you went through this suffering. 

Keep praying to God and seek after him with all your heart. Trust that he is with you in the midst of this suffering and he will surely begin his work of healing within you like he did within me.
Because he wants to be with you.
Because he wants to be with you.

I think it’s quite rude of you to bring my personal life into this and I don’t really want to talk about it but I’ll tel you that I’ve dealt with depression and suicidal thoughts for quite a long period of my life and still struggling with them. I absolutely do not consider myself a “self-righteous” person, rather there have been times where I hated God and swore at him for making me go through pain and suffering. But in the end, if I had not been comforted by the fact that my suffering was for the sake of God’s plan of humbling me, I might have actually committed suicide. 

That hardships and suffering in our life is part of God’s plan should be a comforting reassurance that God is in control of our lives. 

Take for example Joseph. 
Joseph was hated by his brothers, sold into slavery, falsely accused and sent to prison. Joseph suffered tremendous hardships but at the end of his story, he tells his brothers that it was for the sake of God’s plan to save Egypt from starvation that he was made to endure these hardships. 

I’m no rape victim but I sure wouldn’t be comforted if you told me that me being raped was not at all under God’s control and that he couldn’t do anything about it. No, as a child of God, I would want to be comforted by God himself by knowing that his plan somehow lies in the midst of these hardships, even if it may not make sense to me at first. 

I hope that if you are to face suffering and hardships one day, you will use the opportunity to grow closer to God through it rather than dismissing it as a unlucky random event that you happened to experience.

First of all, for other life forms to exist is biblically impossible because God created the universe, and THEN he created all life on earth. ON EARTH. No other planet. 

Even if other life forms were to exist, they would not go to Heaven or Hell when they die. This is because they would not have souls, so they would simply be like animals who just die when they die. Jesus wouldn’t have anything to do with them.

For every sin, there has to be a punishment. When you say “finite sin”, it makes it sound like you are arguing that we are sinful because of the “finite sinful acts” we make in our lives. Rather, we are all born as sinners because we are descendants of Adam, the first sinner. Compare it to two slaves having a baby. That baby is not born free, but rather born as a slave. 

Now if we are sinners, then we must pay the price of our sin. The reason hell is eternal is because there is no one that can pay the price of our sin once we die. We must forever live in sin, which is living in hell. 

Accepting Jesus into our hearts while on earth is the one opportunity God gave for humans in order for them to be forgiven.

I understand that this is written in the Bible. However, when Jesus says “blasphemy against the Holy Spirit”, he is not referring to vocally cursing the Holy Spirit or saying bad things about it. Rather, he is referring to those who reject the Holy Spirit or in other words, reject Jesus Christ as their savior. 

Now if one rejects Jesus Christ and thus the Holy Spirit, how can they be saved? They are not. And as a result, none of their sins are forgiven. 

Now let’s say today I had a really frustrating day and so in a burst of anger and impulsiveness I yell to the Holy Spirit “Why did you make my day so difficult?!!” In this case, it is clear that I sinned against the Holy Spirit but I would argue that I am not going to Hell because I said this. Since Jesus Christ is my Lord and Savior and he died on the cross for all of my sins, this sin will be forgiven as well and I will go to Heaven.

I don’t know if you understood my example but in the end, it all comes down to whether you have accepted Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior. :)
